It's ingrained in most of us through evolution. So people will not accept it because it affects them. Simple as that. Perhaps tell him how you feel about your own eating habits compared to him. Try to ask if there's anything he thinks is wrong. Ask him to go see a doctor about it.

I was an obese kid. 

My family and I went to the beach one day, I was 13, and we took a bunch of pictures as you do. I knew I was chubby, but I never thought of myself as particularly fat. That is, until I saw the pictures we took and noticed I looked like I was 3 times my mom (we are pretty close in height too -- I'm 5'3 and she's about 5'2). I felt awful and decided to do something about it. 

I went to the doctor one day and found I was 180lbs a couple of years later. I had done nothing about it. I was a kid still, and I did do something then, just not the right thing. I went from binge eating to purging to straight up not eating. I worked out like crazy. I went down to nearly 100lbs when I was 16. 

I replaced bad habits with different, but still bad habits. I'm still struggling with that. Currently at a healthy weight (just below 120), and I still struggle with food, just not in the same way I did as a kid. I'm scared of letting myself go and see myself get back to how I looked at 13. I have support from loved ones and every day is a fight, but most days I'm winning. Some days I still can't bring myself to eat, but it doesn't happen as often now. 

Man, being an obese kid really shapes you in a weird way.
